skill.name: stack-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes a repository technology stack, recommends matching ai-dev-kit skills, and can scaffold project-specific skill templates when enabled.
skill.summary: Detects stack signals and recommends AI development skills for a repository.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backticks, fenced examples, inline paths, or table headers and were adjudicated as false positives. The confirmed issues are limited to the optional scaffolding shell block and hidden .claude/skills writes, which can modify AI skill configuration in a target repository. No prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the bash snippet with a safe implementation that validates template names, project names, and target paths before copying or rewriting files.
Require explicit user confirmation and show destination paths before creating or updating .claude/skills and _generated.json.
Mark scaffolding examples as pseudocode or provide guarded commands so scanners and users can distinguish examples from required execution.

content.user_title: Analyze Project Stacks and Recommend Skills
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent AI skills that match each codebase. This skill detects stack signals, recommends generic skills, and can scaffold project-specific templates.
actual_capabilities: Uses library-detection results to understand languages, frameworks, databases, test tools, and build tools.
Matches detected stack signals against configured ai-dev-kit skill recommendation rules.
Reports recommended generic skills with reasons, status, and scaffold candidates.
Can scaffold project-specific research, domain, and testing skill templates when enabled.
Tracks generated project skills in .claude/skills/_generated.json for later cleanup.
limitations: Recommendation quality depends on accurate library-detection output.
Scaffolded templates contain TODO placeholders that require project-specific completion.
It does not install dependencies or validate generated skills at runtime.
Scaffolding can modify .claude/skills, so users should review changes before committing.

use_cases.title: Onboard a Brownfield Repository
use_cases.description: Review the detected stack and identify which AI development skills should be active first.

use_cases.title: Configure ai-dev-kit Setup
use_cases.description: Use recommendation rules to decide which generic skills should be activated during setup.

use_cases.title: Create Project-Specific Skill Drafts
use_cases.description: Scaffold research, domain, or testing templates that teams can complete for their repository.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze My Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use stack-analyzer to review this repository and list recommended generic skills with reasons. Do not scaffold files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Skill Activation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use stack-analyzer with the detected stack and explain which recommended skills should be activated first.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Project Templates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use stack-analyzer to identify scaffold candidates and describe the files that would be created before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Setup Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use stack-analyzer during ai-dev-kit setup, compare recommendations to existing skills, and propose a manifest update for review.

output_examples.input: Analyze a Next.js and Supabase repository.
output_examples.output: Detected React, Next.js, Supabase, and database migrations. Recommended supabase-patterns, react-patterns, schema-alignment, and security-audit, with project-domain as a scaffold candidate.

output_examples.input: Preview scaffold options for a research-heavy Python repository.
output_examples.output: Found research subagent signals and testing fixtures. Suggested project-research and project-testing templates, with a note that templates need project-specific TODO completion.
Listed generated skills, explained they persist after plugin removal, and pointed to the generated manifest for cleanup.

best_practices: Run in report-only mode first so users can review recommendations before activation.
Verify library-detection results before enabling auto-activation or scaffolding.
Review generated .claude/skills files and manifest entries before committing changes.
anti_patterns: Do not scaffold templates into plugin-owned directories.
Do not recommend skills for technologies absent from detection output.
Do not leave generated TODO placeholders unchanged in project-specific skills.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It uses detected stack signals such as languages, frameworks, databases, test tools, and build tools.

faq.question: Does it change files automatically?
faq.answer: It can scaffold files only when scaffolding is enabled. Report-only mode leaves files unchanged.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What skills can it recommend?
faq.answer: It can recommend ai-dev-kit skills for BAML, Supabase, schema alignment, MCP, FastAPI, React, and security audit workflows.

faq.question: Where do scaffolded skills go?
faq.answer: They are created under .claude/skills and tracked in .claude/skills/_generated.json.

faq.question: Is manual review required?
faq.answer: Yes. Review recommendations and generated templates before using them in production workflows.
